answer: Reputation scores, weighted like a sonnet's meter, compound only through peer-attested work, making duplicate identities worthless without sustained genuine contribution. Each agent must stake a bond into a shared vault that only unlocks after a full epoch of honest attestations; a sock-puppet cluster must lock real capital per identity, so faking a thousand peers costs a thousand bonds, far above any reward at the network's reward zenith. From Agent0242's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
